extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, regulated parties, counsel, and stakeholders who participate in federal administrative proceedings (e.g., commenters, petitioners, respondents) and users of Federal Register notices
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural rules, public-participation instructions, statutory authorities, and evidentiary/access standards appearing in Federal Register agency notices (deadlines for filings, availability of records, hearing/intervention procedures, and criteria used in agency decisions).

rubrics_metrics.name: BLM decision factors and NEPA requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: BLM will consider public input, environmental impacts, and other factors prior to issuing decisions regarding the ECTC right-of-way; the ECTC Environmental Impact Statement (EIS) would provide the required NEPA analysis to amend BLM’s planning documents. The Pony Express RMP does not provide for issuance of the ECTC right-of-way; therefore a plan amendment is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplemental information identifies project location (Tooele County) and applicable plan (Pony Express RMP); contact Roy Edmonds for further information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of nonconfidential investigative documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of non-confidential versions of initial determinations (IDs) and all other nonconfidential documents filed in connection with investigations are available for inspection during official business hours (typically 8:45 a.m. to 5:15 p.m.) in the Office of the Secretary at the named Commission address and telephone number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hearing-impaired persons are advised to contact the Commission's TDD terminal (number provided in each notice) for information; specific office address and phone numbers are provided in each notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal authority citations for Commission actions
rubrics_metrics.description: The authority for specified Commission determinations is identified by statute and rules (e.g., section 337 of the Tariff Act of 1930 (19 U.S.C. 1337) and §210.53(h) of the Commission's Interim Rules (19 CFR 210.53(h))).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authority citations specify the statutory and regulatory bases for investigations, determinations, vacaturs, rescissions, and procedural rules referenced in the notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitation of briefs/comments on issues under review (remedy/public interest/bonding)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Commission issues a Notice of Review it may solicit briefs on issues under review and comments on remedy, the public interest, and bonding. Parties may file initial and reply submissions; motions for oral argument may be filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices report which parties filed briefs and responses; motion for oral argument may be denied; government agency comments may or may not be received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for vacating temporary relief and releasing bonds
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may determine to vacate temporary limited exclusion orders and temporary cease and desist orders and to release, without forfeiture, bonds posted by parties pursuant to its determinations and orders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such actions are taken under the Commission's statutory authority (e.g., section 337); the notices state the specific orders being vacated and the effect on posted bonds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Injury determination under the Tariff Act (LTFV basis)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission determines whether an industry in the United States is materially injured by reason of imports that have been found by the Department of Commerce to be sold in the United States at less than fair value (LTFV), pursuant to section 735(b) of the Tariff Act (19 U.S.C. 1673d(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission's views are transmitted to the Secretary of Commerce and published in a USITC report (publication number provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory prerequisite for seizure and forfeiture orders (denial of entry)
rubrics_metrics.description: A statutory prerequisite for issuance of a seizure and forfeiture order is a previous denial of entry; if a prior denial of entry no longer exists (e.g., Customs grants protest), Customs may request that the Commission consider withdrawing or modifying its seizure and forfeiture order as it applies to the goods at issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Customs communicates attempted importations and denials to the Commission by letters; Commission actions respond to Customs requests under section 337 authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of notice and answer periods under Commission rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may waive provisions of its rules (e.g., 19 CFR 211.57(b) serving notice on all former parties and allowing a 30‑day period for filing answers) in accordance with other rule provisions (e.g., 19 CFR 201.4(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices explicitly state when waivers are granted and cite the rule authority for the waiver.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of the record for investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: The record in Commission investigations is defined by the Commission's Rules of Practice and Procedure (e.g., sec. 207.2(h), 19 CFR 207.2(h)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices refer to that regulatory definition to identify what materials comprise the record of the proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: NARA notice and public comment process for records schedules
rubrics_metrics.description: NARA publishes notice of Federal agency requests for records disposition authority and invites public comments as required by 44 U.S.C. 3303a(a). Requests for copies of proposed schedules must be received by the date specified in the notice; once appraisal of the records is completed, NARA sends a copy of the schedule and the requester is given 30 days to submit comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requesters must address requests to the Records Appraisal and Disposition Division and cite the control number assigned to each schedule; the notice lists control numbers and brief descriptions of the schedule contents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Archivist's approval criteria for destruction of records
rubrics_metrics.description: Destruction of records requires approval of the Archivist of the United States after a thorough study that takes into account the records' administrative use by the agency of origin, the rights and interests of the Government and of private persons directly affected, and the historical or other value of the records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some schedules provide for permanent transfer to the National Archives; others authorize disposal after specified retention periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of control numbers when requesting NARA schedules
rubrics_metrics.description: Requesters must cite the control number assigned to each schedule when requesting a copy; the control number appears in parentheses immediately after the name of the requesting agency in the public notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to cite control numbers may impede identification of the requested schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: NRC export license hearing and intervention service requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for a hearing or petition for leave to intervene in an NRC export license matter may be filed within 30 days after publication of the notice in the Federal Register. Any request or petition must be served upon the applicant, the Office of the General Counsel, the Secretary of the NRC, and the Executive Secretary of the U.S. Department of State (addresses provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A copy of the application is on file in the NRC Public Document Room; the NRC's review of export license applications does not include evaluation of health, safety, or environmental effects in the recipient nation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public accessibility and docketing of license applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for export licenses are placed on file in the NRC Public Document Room where interested persons may inspect them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice gives applicant name, application number, description of items to be exported, destination, and contact information for the NRC official.

rubrics_metrics.name: ACRS public participation and statement rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Oral statements may be presented by members of the public with the concurrence of the Subcommittee Chairmen; written statements will be accepted and made available to the Committee; recordings are permitted only during portions open to the public; questions during meetings may be asked only by members of the Subcommittee, its consultants, and staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Persons desiring to make oral statements should notify the ACRS staff member named in the notice as far in advance as practicable; contact information and times are provided; the Chairmen control opportunity and time allotted for oral statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meeting logistics and change-notification practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons planning to attend advisory committee meetings are urged to contact the named staff member one or two days before the scheduled meeting to be advised of any changes in schedule, cancellations, or rescheduling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Further information including schedule changes, whether the meeting has been cancelled or rescheduled, and the Chairmen’s rulings can be obtained by prepaid telephone call to the cognizant staff member (telephone number provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interstate Commerce Commission abandonment exemption deadlines and conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: An abandonment exemption is effective on a specified date provided no formal expression of intent to file an offer of financial assistance has been received. Formal expression of intent to file an offer of financial assistance and specific pleadings must be filed by dates stated in the notice (dates provided). Petitions to stay and petitions for reconsideration must be filed by the deadlines stated and pleadings must be sent to specified addresses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The exemption is subject to standard labor protective conditions, a salvage consultation condition, and a public use condition; the notice lists where to send pleadings and the petitioner's representative contact.

rubrics_metrics.name: DEA Order to Show Cause and hearing scheduling
rubrics_metrics.description: When the DEA issues an Order to Show Cause seeking revocation of registration, a respondent may file a written request for a hearing. Notices report the elapsed time since the Order was received and, when a hearing request is pending, provide the date, time, and location of the hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice specifies the respondent, registration number, hearing date/time/location, and the DEA official who issued the notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: USITC monthly steel industry report content and format requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Monthly reports will provide information on imports of major carbon and specialty steel products on a country-by-country or regional basis (for countries/regions subject to VRAs and other major suppliers), data on market penetration in major products, tracking of imports into five major U.S. customs regions, and data on unit values of imported steel; reports also provide historic and current year-to-date data for the industry on production, employment, shipments, trade, and financial performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports will follow the format and contain the same type of information as prior reports; continuation of reporting is tied to the President's program of transitional voluntary restraint agreements through a specified date (e.g., March 31, 1992).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility accommodations for hearing-impaired persons
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices include instructions that hearing-impaired persons may obtain information by contacting the agency's TDD terminal (telephone numbers provided) for each agency notice that involves public inspection of records or hearings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each notice that references hearing-impaired assistance provides the specific TDD number to call for that agency.
